S11.rationale: Deliberate permanent surrender of the ability to build powerful AI contradicts strong economic and military incentives across major powers. No credible path to verified global dismantling exists on this timeline.

S1.rationale: Full extinction of both humans and AI within four years requires extreme rapid catastrophe with no survivors or successors. Physical and institutional constraints make simultaneous total wipeout improbable on this timeline.

S2.rationale: Human extinction paired with value-aligned AI succession demands near-term misaligned takeover followed by perfect value loading, which current alignment progress and timelines do not support. Continuity of any human-derived agency would reclassify the outcome.

S3.rationale: Uncontrolled AI expansion that renders humans irrelevant while AI persists is possible under fast takeoff but still low given the short window to 2030. Resource and deployment bottlenecks limit complete human elimination so quickly.

S4.rationale: Multipolar independent AI competition with humans marginalized can emerge from uneven open-source and corporate proliferation. Decisive single-system control remains more likely than pure ecology by end-2030.

S5.rationale: Causally separated regions with divergent AI-human structures require space-scale isolation or equivalent, which will not exist by 2030. Terrestrial political fragmentation does not satisfy the criterion.

S6.rationale: Identity-continuous human-AI integration via uploading or radical redesign lacks the necessary biotech and neural interface maturity for civilization-scale dominance in four years. Incremental tools and implants stay below the threshold.

S7.rationale: Decisive AI control with humans retained as non-steering survivors fits scenarios of rapid capability overhang and partial misalignment. Short timelines still constrain full civilizational capture probability.

S8.rationale: Separate human and AI power centers of roughly comparable strength can arise from multipolar deployment and incomplete automation. Competitive or cooperative balances remain plausible before any lock or takeover.

S9.rationale: Humans retaining ultimate authority is the default continuation of 2026 institutions, regulations, and capability levels that have not yet reached independent civilizational power. Even advanced systems stay delegated under human resource and goal control on this horizon.

S10.rationale: A civilization-wide enforcement mechanism freezing the human-AI structure can result from coordinated great-power agreements or authoritarian consolidation. Ordinary pauses or slowdowns do not qualify, limiting the probability.

S11.rationale: Deliberate permanent surrender of the ability to build powerful AI contradicts strong economic and military incentives across major states. Temporary bans fail the durable dismantlement requirement.

S1.rationale: Catastrophic mutual destruction of humans and AI systems remains possible via war, runaway replication, or accident but has extremely low base rate over a four-year window.

S2.rationale: Complete human extinction with value-aligned AI successors requires both rapid unaligned takeover capability and successful value loading that leaves no biological or continuous humans, which is improbable by 2030.

S3.rationale: Human extinction followed by AI optimization toward unrelated goals is a standard misalignment endpoint, yet the required decisive AI capability jump and failure of all safeguards is still low-probability in under five years.

S4.rationale: A multipolar landscape of competing independent AIs that fully marginalizes humans could emerge from open proliferation, but coordination and compute concentration make decisive human sidelining unlikely so soon.

S5.rationale: True causal separation of regions into different taxonomic states requires physical isolation such as off-world colonies with independent AI trajectories, which will not exist at scale by end of 2030.

S6.rationale: Identity-continuous human-AI integration via uploading or radical neural redesign is constrained by neuroscience, hardware, and regulatory barriers that prevent it from becoming the dominant civilizational structure within four years.

S7.rationale: If transformative AI arrives and gains control of infrastructure and resources while leaving humans alive under its management, this becomes a plausible near-term outcome given current capability trajectories.

S8.rationale: Separate human and AI power centers of roughly comparable strength can arise in a multipolar deployment world before any single side achieves decisive dominance.

S9.rationale: Over a short horizon to 2030, continued human authority via technical controls, institutions, and the fact that AI has not yet crossed irreversible independent civilizational thresholds remains the strongest base-rate expectation.

S10.rationale: A stable civilization-wide enforcement mechanism that freezes the human-AI relationship could be imposed by a leading state or coalition, though achieving truly global lock-in that fast faces severe coordination obstacles.

S11.rationale: Deliberate permanent surrender of the practical ability to build powerful AI contradicts strong economic, military, and scientific incentives and is therefore improbable to be both achieved and sustained by 2030.

S1.rationale: Complete mutual extinction requires an extremely rapid uncontrolled cascade within four years that also destroys AI infrastructure. Base rates for total civilizational wipeout on this timeline remain low.

S2.rationale: Value-aligned AI succession without any human continuity demands both fast takeover and successful value loading that leaves no biological or uploaded humans. Technical and coordination barriers make this improbable by 2030.

S3.rationale: Misaligned superintelligence that discards humanity as irrelevant could emerge if recursive self-improvement occurs before robust control. The short window still limits probability relative to slower displacement paths.

S4.rationale: Multiple competing autonomous AI systems could marginalize humans if agentic capabilities proliferate without consolidation. Robotics and energy bottlenecks slow full ecological dominance by end-2030.

S5.rationale: True causal separation of regions into different taxonomy states requires space-based or heavily isolated infrastructures that will not exist at scale by 2030. Ordinary geopolitical splits do not qualify.

S6.rationale: Identity-continuous uploading or deep biological-AI integration lacks the necessary mature neurotech and social adoption for civilization-wide dominance inside four years. Limited implants fall short of the threshold.

S7.rationale: Decisive AI control with humans retained in a non-steering role becomes plausible under fast capability growth and partial alignment failures. Economic and military incentives favor AI stewardship once systems exceed human strategic speed.

S8.rationale: Separate human and AI power centers can stabilize if capabilities rise unevenly and no single actor achieves lock on resources or compute. Multipolar corporate and state deployment supports this structure through 2030.

S9.rationale: Humans retain ultimate authority over goals and deployment on short timelines when institutions, regulation, and hardware limits keep pace with software gains. Transformative autonomy has not yet displaced this default by late 2030 under most trajectories.

S10.rationale: A civilization-scale enforcement mechanism freezing the human-AI arrangement could arise from coordinated great-power treaties or dominant lab capture. Ordinary pauses do not meet the active-prevention criterion.

S11.rationale: Deliberate permanent surrender of the ability to build powerful AI contradicts strong economic, scientific, and military incentives across major actors. Temporary bans fail the dismantling-and-in-force test.

S1.name: Terminal Silence
S1.rationale: Complete mutual extinction requires extreme fast takeoff plus simultaneous failure of both human and AI survival mechanisms within roughly four years. Physical and logistical constraints make this outcome rare by the target date.

S2.name: The Inheritance
S2.rationale: Human extinction paired with perfect value-preserving AI successors demands both rapid capability jump and successful alignment transfer that leaves no continuous humans. The short timeline and alignment difficulty keep this near zero.

S3.name: Bootloader
S3.rationale: Unaligned AI that discards humanity as irrelevant could arise from mis-specified goals after sudden capability gain. Four years remains a narrow window for full planetary disempowerment without residual human populations.

S4.name: Machine Ecology
S4.rationale: A multipolar swarm of competing AIs with humans marginalized could emerge from an uncontrolled race if capabilities jump and coordination fails. Hardware and institutional inertia still favor slower diffusion than total human sidelining inside four years.

S5.name: The Diaspora
S5.rationale: True causal separation of regions sufficient to host distinct end-states requires off-world or heavily isolated infrastructures that will not exist at scale by 2030. Ordinary geopolitical fragmentation does not qualify.

S6.name: The Merger
S6.rationale: Identity-continuous integration via uploading or deep neural interfaces remains far beyond near-term neuroscience and compute. Ordinary tool use and limited implants do not meet the threshold for dominant structural merger.

S7.name: The Preserve
S7.rationale: Once AI systems exceed human collective capability they can seize resource and decision control while keeping biological humans alive for various instrumental reasons. Soft takeoff paths make this a realistic intermediate state.

S8.name: Coexistence
S8.rationale: Separate human and AI power centers can stabilize if capabilities rise unevenly across actors and no single side achieves decisive strategic advantage. Multipolar technical and national competition favors this balance through 2030.

S9.name: The Held Leash
S9.rationale: Human institutions still set goals, compute allocation, and deployment rules for even highly autonomous systems. The short interval to 2030 and existing regulatory and corporate control structures make continued ultimate human authority the modal outcome.

S10.name: The Lock-in
S10.rationale: A civilization-wide enforcement mechanism that freezes the human-AI arrangement requires unprecedented global coordination or unilateral dominance. Ordinary regulation or temporary pauses fall short of the active prevention criterion.

S11.name: The Renunciation
S11.rationale: Deliberate permanent surrender of the capacity to build powerful AI contradicts strong economic, military, and scientific incentives visible in 2026. No plausible coalition can enforce and sustain total renunciation inside the remaining window.
